picks.what: Panorama, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored profile view of the whole town with St. John’s; the ’s-Hertogenbosch strip of the vol. 1 three-city plate (with Leuven and Mechelen); yellow frame trimmed, the text cartouche at lower right stays outside a 16:9 crop

picks.what: St. John’s Cathedral above the rooftops, lithograph (Rijksmuseum)
picks.why: St. John’s tower and dome rising over trees and roofs; Rijksmuseum dates it only to the printmaker’s working years; margins trimmed

picks.file: NIMH - 2011 - 3616 - Aerial photograph of 's-Hertogenbosch, The Netherlands.jpg
picks.what: Aerial photograph of St. John’s Cathedral (NIMH)
picks.why: the cathedral and surrounding streets from the air; cleaner copy than #19, which has a scratch across it; black border trimmed

gaps: P0: nothing; P2: nothing usable; P4: nothing firmly dated; P6: no good modern view
notes: #2 is the colored top strip of the Braun and Hogenberg vol. 1 plate that also shows Leuven and Mechelen, so dated 1572 rather than the 1575–84 on Commons; #4 (Beudeker atlas) pairs the vol. 4 plan with the same strip. The vol. 4 plan (#1), Blaeu’s plans (#3, #5, #8, #9), Merian’s fortification plan (#10) and de Wit’s plan (#7) are plans rather than views. P2: #14 is a 1900–03 photograph of Adam Frans van der Meulen’s 1672 panorama drawing, a true view but badly stained; usable as a last resort with y 1672. #11 is another impression of #12, with a blank sky. P4: Vertin’s painting of the Markt and town hall (#16) is dated only ‘by 1893’ (his death year), and the ‘Nederland in Beeld’ collotype of St. John’s (#15) only 1875–1930; both good pictures if a date can be confirmed. #13 and #18 are cathedral interiors. Modern: 2006 balloon photos show suburbs, a golf-course castle (#23) or the town too hazy to make out (#24).
